title: Optimal substructure

overview.what: A problem has optimal substructure if an optimal solution to it contains optimal solutions to its subproblems.
overview.why: It tells you that cached sub-answers can be safely combined to form the final correct answer.

why_learning_this: It is the second diagnostic test to confirm if a problem is a DP problem.
Together with overlapping subproblems, this proves that breaking a problem down and caching its pieces will yield the mathematically correct optimal answer.

common_mistakes.title: Conflating overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure
common_mistakes.explanation: They are different properties. Overlapping subproblems means caching helps performance. Optimal substructure means the problem can be solved by combining optimal sub-answers. Both are required for DP.

common_mistakes.title: Assuming all path problems have it
common_mistakes.explanation: Shortest simple path has optimal substructure (a sub-path of a shortest path is also shortest). Longest simple path does NOT have optimal substructure, because the sub-paths cannot be independently combined without creating cycles.

recall_questions.q: What does it mean for a problem to have optimal substructure?
recall_questions.answer: An optimal solution to the overall problem can be constructed directly from optimal solutions to its subproblems.

recall_questions.q: What two properties must a problem have to be solvable by Dynamic Programming?

practice_tasks.title: Shortest Path composition
practice_tasks.prompt: Modify this recursive shortest-path function to return not just the distance, but the path itself, demonstrating that the optimal path is built from optimal sub-paths.

understanding_checks.question: If a problem has overlapping subproblems but lacks optimal substructure, can you use DP?
understanding_checks.answer: No. You can cache the subproblems (overlapping), but combining those cached answers won't give you the correct optimal answer for the larger problem (lacks optimal substructure).
understanding_checks.why: DP requires both properties: caching to save time, and optimal substructure for correctness.

understanding_checks.question: A classmate says: 'Merge sort uses optimal substructure because it combines two sorted halves to sort the full array. That makes it DP.' Why are they wrong?
understanding_checks.answer: They are correct that merge sort has optimal substructure. However, it lacks overlapping subproblems (every recursive call sorts a unique portion of the array). Therefore, DP caching doesn't help.
understanding_checks.why: Optimal substructure is required for DP, but it is also present in Divide and Conquer algorithms. The lack of overlapping subproblems is why merge sort isn't DP.

challenge.title: Longest Simple Path
challenge.prompt: Explain why the longest simple path problem does not have optimal substructure.
challenge.solution: The longest simple path from A to C might be A->B->C. However, the longest simple path from A to B could use nodes that are also required to go from B to C. Because paths cannot revisit nodes, the subproblems are not independent and cannot simply be combined.
